 3   act to amend the Highway Law.

12   Marchione to explain her vote.

13                SENATOR MARCHIONE:   Thank you, 

14   Mr. President.  

15                I rise for the purpose of speaking 

16   on this legislation before us.  I'm truly honored 

17   to sponsor this bill designating the overpass at 

18   Exit 14 of Route 87 North as the Assemblyman 

19   Robert D'Andrea Bridge.  

20                Naming a bridge in Saratoga County 

21   after Assemblyman Robert "Bobby" D'Andrea truly 

22   benefits his legacy of honorable, thoughtful 

23   public service.  

24                Because whether he was serving as 

25   supervisor for the City of Saratoga Springs or in 


                                                                1410

 1   the State Assembly, where he did for 27 years, 

 2   the true hallmark of Bobby D'Andrea is a service 

 3   of building bridges:  Bridges of opportunity and 

 4   inclusion for the betterment of everyone; bridges 

 5   of kindness, cooperation, and collegiality to 

 6   advance the greater good.  Those bridges, built 

 7   upon a strong foundation of tireless community 

 8   service and dedicated charitable involvement, led 

 9   the way for a brighter future.

10                Bobby D'Andrea's life, Bobby 

11   D'Andrea's legacy, they transcended politics.  

12   Always ready, willing and able to roll up his 

13   sleeves and do the hard work, the real work of 

14   public service, Bobby D'Andrea has resided in the 

15   City of Saratoga Springs east of Interstate 87 at 

16   Exit 14 for decades.  And now this nearby bridge 

17   will bear the name of a true bridge builder, 

18   Bobby D'Andrea, to celebrate his honorable legacy 

19   of service to our Saratoga-Washington community.  

20                I congratulate Bobby, his wife 

21   Theresa, their five children and six 

22   grandchildren on this designation.  

23                Thank you.

24                ACTING PRESIDENT BOYLE:   Thank you, 

25   Senator.  Bobby was a great man.

24                SENATOR ESPAILLAT:   Thank you, 

25   Mr. President.  I rise to explain my vote.  


                                                                1416

 1                The history of farmworker 

 2   disenfranchisement is rooted in the Jim Crow era.  

 3   And sadly, their unfair treatment continues to be 

 4   a lasting legacy of those times.  

 5                Farmworkers toil in hard conditions 

 6   from sunup to sundown to feed all of us.  The 

 7   conditions they work in are often harsh and often 

 8   unsafe.  The conditions they live in are often 

 9   unsanitary.  And yet farmworkers do not have 

10   access to workers' compensation, and they are not 

11   allowed to organize.  

12                The treatment of farmworkers is 

13   abhorrent and unacceptable.  And I, along with 

14   many others, have advocated to end these shameful 

15   practices that are a moral affront to everything 

16   our state stands for.  

17                As we get ready to approve next 

18   year's budget this week, let's be sure not to 

19   leave our farmworkers once again.  Let's get $15 

20   an hour, let's be the first to do it, and let's 

21   make sure farmworkers get in there too.

22                This is one of many bills that will 

23   give the farm industry handsome benefits, and I, 

24   as I've done in the last several years, will 

25   continue to vote down on all of them.  My vote is 


                                                                1417

 1   in the negative, Mr. President.

 7                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

 8   Resolution Number 3192, by Senator Venditto, 

 9   congratulating C.J. Marie of North Bellmore, 

10   New York, upon the occasion of being named 2015 

11   Ms. New York Senior America.

12                ACTING PRESIDENT BOYLE:   Senator 

13   Venditto.

14                SENATOR VENDITTO:   Mr. President, 

15   thank you very much.  

16                I have the distinct honor of 

17   introducing a very important and distinguished 

18   guest to our chamber today.  Her name is C.J. 

19   Marie, and she is also known as Ms. New York 

20   Senior America.

21                You know, whatever side of the 

22   political ledger we may stand on, ladies and 

23   gentlemen, I think we can all agree that the men 

24   and women who are members of our senior 

25   population here in New York State, they have made 


                                                                1420

 1   great sacrifices to build, cultivate and maintain 

 2   the communities where we live and raise our 

 3   families.  

 4                And they also helped pave the way 

 5   for all of us to enjoy the freedoms, the 

 6   privileges and the opportunities that we have 

 7   each and every day.  They're continuing to work 

 8   to make sure that those freedoms, privileges and 

 9   opportunities are preserved for generations to 

10   come.  

11                And we have with us today a terrific 

12   spokeswoman for our senior population in New York 

13   in Ms. Marie.  She has amassed a tremendous 

14   amount of professional success in her life:  a 

15   teacher of over 35 years at the elementary school 

16   level.  She has written, get this, 14 books, all 

17   of which provide valuable lessons for living.  

18   She has dedicated a great part of her life to 

19   physical fitness and dance and sharing what she's 

20   learned in those fields with others so that they 

21   can better their lives.  The accomplishments just 

22   go on and on.

23                And on a personal level, she has 

24   also achieved so much success, using her time, 

25   her talents, her treasures -- and, yes, her 


                                                                1421

 1   beauty -- to travel across the state to help 

 2   people, particularly those who are most in need.

 3                So, Ms. Marie, on behalf of all my 

 4   colleagues, I would like to welcome you to the 

 5   chamber today and thank you for being with us.  

 6                Ladies and gentlemen, the one and 

 7   only Ms. New York Senior America, C.J. Marie.
